description:
Found while profiling the compiler (2026-10-20).

Problem: the method in use (a temporary :timer.tc around Defk.Compiler.compile in Defk.__before_compile__, summed over a mix dump_c round) includes waiting. mix dump_c runs compile --force, so lib and test/support compile in parallel, and the first kernel module (Examples.Kernels, test/support/examples.ex) waits about 1 s for the compiler's own modules. Of a 2.5 s round, about 1.0 s is that wait; the same module needs 13 ms warm. Warm, the real work over all 116 modules is about 1.4-1.5 s (single rounds vary about 10% on the laptop). Percentages measured the old way are diluted by the wait, so the chain's +14.1% (of the 15% ceiling, ADR-0007 Consequences: Cost) is probably more of the real work.

Do:
- A dev harness for compiler time, so no step needs a temporary patch: per module, compile once (warm-up), then time a second Defk.Compiler.compile; write module and microseconds to a log (for example DEFK_COMPILE_TIME=<file> read in __before_compile__, or a dev/ script). Keep it out of HexDocs and the user's path; it must cost nothing when off.
- Measure the chain again with it: main at 23e27970 (before step 1) against current main, three rounds interleaved, total and total without SatEx.Kernels.
- Record the corrected numbers in docs/performance.md (the compiler-time entries 6.32 onward) and ADR-0007's cost note; say what the old method measured.

Owner, 2026-10-20: measure first, then the copy-analysis cut (defk-o08.3, blocked by this ticket). The new numbers show how much of the 15% ceiling is left.

Gate: mix ci; PR per AGENTS.md.
title: Compiler time: measure warm compiles, and measure the symbolic-bounds chain again against its budget
